response.headline: The service measures poorly here, but no single cause reaches a strong level [insufficient_data].

causes.explanation: Speed evidence rests on only 2-3 tests [speed_cell][speed_1km], one nearby site's operators are unknown [operators_5km], and antenna heights are assumed or inferred for O2 and Vodafone [los_o2][los_vodafone]. The evidence cannot separate distance, terrain, or single-operator causes at the point.

Measured speeds are far below the UK median [speed_cell][speed_1km], while neighbours are much faster [speed_neighbours]. EE and Three have clear lines about 1 km away [los_ee][los_three], so distance alone is not a strong explanation; O2 and Vodafone sites are farther and terrain-weakened [los_o2][los_vodafone], but antenna heights are assumed or inferred, keeping this at or below 0.5.

Terrain rises above the direct line to O2 and Vodafone sites [los_o2][los_vodafone], likely weakening those signals, but EE and Three have clear lines [los_ee][los_three]. Antenna heights are assumed or inferred, so terrain cannot be confirmed as the point-level cause and stays at or below 0.5.

Only EE, O2 and Three have sites within 5 km, and one nearby site's operators are unknown [operators_5km]; EE and Three have clear lines [los_ee][los_three] while O2 and Vodafone are weakened [los_o2][los_vodafone]. This suggests uneven operator coverage but does not prove only one operator serves the point, so confidence stays low.

actions.text: Try EE or Three, which have clear lines of sight to nearby sites [network_comparison][los_ee][los_three].
Use Wi-Fi calling indoors if mobile signal is weak.
Check your address on Ofcom's mobile coverage checker: https://www.ofcom.org.uk/mobile-coverage-checker
Emergency calls work on any available network.

response.best_network: EE is likely best, with Three also clear; O2 and Vodafone are likely weaker.
limitations: Sites are approximate; antenna heights are assumed or inferred for some operators; Ofcom coverage figures are area-level, not point-specific.
Causes are inferred from public data, not confirmed: operators' network data is not public.
Ookla speeds are quarterly aggregates with no time-of-day detail; congestion can only be inferred.
No address-level Ofcom coverage; Ofcom figures are for the whole constituency and are predictions.
Mast sites are approximate (crowd-sourced OpenCelliD, OpenStreetMap, Ofcom's licence register) and incomplete, so 'no sites found' is weak evidence.
Line of sight uses a surface model (trees and buildings included) and mostly assumed antenna heights; blocked means a weaker signal, not no signal.
